Resources

Good resources, in one place.

Resources for people who are blind or have low vision are scattered across the internet. We’ve gathered the ones we know, use, and recommend in one place, organized around what you want to do.

  • New to vision loss
  • Work and careers
  • Technology help
  • Community and advocacy
  • Reading and media

New to vision loss

Hadley ↗

Free courses and workshops designed for adults adjusting to vision loss — practical skills, technology, and everyday living, at your own pace.

VisionAware ↗

Guides and straight answers for living with vision loss, from the American Printing House for the Blind — home, cooking, travel, and getting organized.

APH ConnectCenter ↗

The American Printing House's hub for blindness resources, including a directory of services in your community.

Work and careers

APH CareerConnect ↗

Career guidance for blind and low-vision job seekers — exploring careers, résumés, interviews, and finding work that fits.

Job Accommodation Network ↗

Free, practical guidance on workplace accommodations — written for employees asking and employers offering.

California Department of Rehabilitation ↗

California's vocational rehabilitation agency — training, equipment, and job support when employment is your goal. Every state has its own version.

Technology help

AppleVis ↗

The community for blind Apple users — app reviews, how-to guides, podcasts, and a forum where no question is too small.

Be My Eyes ↗

Free visual help through your phone's camera — sighted volunteers and AI describe what you point it at.

Aira ↗

Trained visual interpreters on demand, by subscription — and covered free at many airports, stores, and campuses.

Community and advocacy

National Federation of the Blind ↗

The largest organization of blind people in the United States — local chapters, community, and a voice in the decisions that affect blind lives.

American Council of the Blind ↗

A national membership and advocacy organization of blind and visually impaired people, with affiliates and chapters across the country.

Reading and media

National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled ↗

Free audiobooks, braille books, and magazines by download and mail, for anyone who cannot read standard print — through your local library.

Bookshare ↗

A large library of accessible ebooks — free for U.S. students, and available to adults by membership.

NFB-NEWSLINE ↗

Newspapers, magazines, and TV listings in audio and braille — free by phone, app, or email for registered readers.

This list is short on purpose — everything here is a resource we know and stand behind. If a link stops working, or you think something belongs on this page, please email us and tell us.
